column1: # Product Backlog. Tab-separated, one card per row. Read by 03-seed.sh.
# Columns: id | type | sprint | owner | points | priority | epic | title | stories | files | branch | acceptance | notes | blocks
# Multi-value cells (stories, files, acceptance, blocks) use ';' as the separator. '-' means empty.
# 'notes' is free prose shown as the ## Notes section of the issue. 'blocks' non-empty marks the card a blocker.
# Lines starting with # are ignored. Do not use tabs inside a cell.

column12: acceptance

column8: Move the SPA into frontend/, update Vite config and Docker paths
column12: npm install and npm run build both succeed from inside frontend/;nothing outside frontend/ imports from src/;the dev server still serves every existing route
column13: The SPA sits at the repository root today, which makes it impossible to give the backend and the frontend separate Dockerfiles. Move it wholesale, then fix the Vite root and the paths in package.json. Do this first - P-01 writes its Dockerfiles against the new layout.

column8: Runtime unblock: add axios, fix the broken api imports, remove the /api/api/ double prefix, enable CORS
column12: A clean npm install in frontend/ succeeds and the app builds;login resolves to /api/auth/login/ with no repeated segment;a browser call from the Vite dev server to the backend is not blocked by CORS;register then log in works end to end in a real browser
column13: Four separate defects stop the app running at all today. (1) axios is imported by services/api.js but is missing from package.json. (2) AuthContext.jsx, Register.jsx and Chat.jsx import '../api' / '../../api', which does not resolve - the file is at src/services/api.js. (3) core/urls.py mounts users.urls under api/ while users/urls.py already declares api/auth/login/, so login actually lives at /api/api/auth/login/ and the client misses it. (4) django-cors-headers is neither installed nor configured. Nothing on the frontend can be wired until all four are fixed.

column8: Backend and frontend Dockerfiles; docker-compose.yml bringing up db + backend + frontend + nginx; .env.example

column13: None of this exists yet. This is the card a grader exercises first - the Sprint-level Definition of Done in execution-plan.md Part 4 is a fresh clone brought up with a single command. Depends on F-01 for the frontend path and pairs with P-03 for the database service.

column8: SQLite to PostgreSQL; settings read from env; requirements.txt; generate the missing Message migration
column12: docker compose up starts Postgres;migrate runs clean on a completely empty database and the messages table exists afterwards;no db.sqlite3 remains tracked;SECRET_KEY and DEBUG come from the environment
column13: settings.py still points at django.db.backends.sqlite3, SECRET_KEY is the hardcoded django-insecure default and DEBUG is True. There is no requirements.txt at all - the implicit deps are django, djangorestframework, djangorestframework-simplejwt, channels, daphne, pillow, plus psycopg[binary] and django-cors-headers. Critically, Message has NO migration: makemigrations was never run after the model was added, so a fresh migrate never creates its table. Postgres is also what US-9.1 needs - full-text search and a GIN index do not exist on SQLite.

column8: Split backend/users/ into the nine modules of architecture.tex section 5
column12: Every module in execution-plan.md Part 7 exists with its models;migrate --plan on an existing database shows no destructive operation;the seed command still runs;no module outside roles decides a permission for itself
column13: Profile, Group, MediaFile and Message all live in one users app today, and every endpoint is in users/views.py. architecture.tex section 5 states nine modules and brief Rule 12 grades that alignment, so one app containing every domain is a visible contradiction of our own design document. Two naming traps: the app must not be called channels (collides with the Django Channels package) nor groups (collides with django.contrib.auth.Group) - use channels_app and groups_app. Move without losing data: set an explicit db_table on each model matching its current table name and use migrations.SeparateDatabaseAndState, then inspect migrate --plan before running it.

column8: Role model with the eight permission booleans, plus migration
column12: A role is a database row, not a code constant;a channel can hold several differently named roles;each role carries all eight booleans;the migration applies clean on an empty database
column13: US-8.1: 'As a channel super-admin, I want to be able to define different roles with different names for users, so that I can structure the management of the channel.' The eight permissions, fixed by user_stories_en.tex section Assumptions, are can_send_media, can_delete_message, can_create_topic, can_edit_channel, can_remove_member, can_add_member, can_change_role, can_delete_channel. Nothing role-shaped exists in the codebase - the only access check anywhere today is group.admin == request.user.

column8: Permission evaluation service has_permission(user, channel, permission), with the channel owner implicitly holding all eight
column12: The check reads database rows, not code;reassigning a role takes effect on the very next request with no restart and no deploy;the channel owner is never refused;a user with no role is refused everything privileged
column13: This is the single most important line in architecture.tex: section 5.1 says no module decides permissions for itself. Messaging, Channels, Groups and Media all call in here. It is what makes brief section 5.8 - access levels manageable without editing code - literally true. If you ever find yourself writing 'if user.id == channel.owner_id' outside this module, stop and call in here instead.

column8: Channel and ChannelMember models and migration
column12: A channel has a name, description, image and owner;ChannelMember joins user to channel and carries a role FK;the migration applies clean;the ERD entities in ERD.tex are matched
column13: US-4.1: 'As a user, I want to be able to create a new channel and become its admin, so that I have a space for discussion, message sharing and file sharing with multiple users.' Nothing channel-shaped exists in the codebase at all. Land the models on day 1 or 2 - four other people's cards are waiting on them. The app directory must be channels_app, not channels, or it collides with the Django Channels package.

column8: Profile model, migration, serializer, and own-profile view/edit endpoint
column12: A user can read and update their own profile and nobody else's;the endpoint refuses an unauthenticated caller;the avatar upload path is under MEDIA_ROOT
column13: US-10.1: 'As a user, I want to have a user profile and be able to edit it, so that I can keep my personal information up to date in the system.' Already written as Profile plus ProfileDetailView in users/. This card is to move it into accounts/ behind P-04, confirm it against the acceptance criteria, get it reviewed and merged through a pull request - it is not Done until it passes the full DoD.

column8: Privacy-settings endpoint toggling allow_invites
column12: The flag defaults to allowing invites;toggling it persists;the flag is readable by the group and channel add-member paths
column13: US-5.4: 'As a user, I want to control who can add me to a group (or channel), so that no one can add me to a group without my permission.' SH.2 is the same requirement from the stakeholder conversation. The endpoint already exists as PrivacySettingsView, but note that GroupAddRemoveMemberView never actually checks the flag - the honouring of it is M-05 and C-04, and this card is what those read.

column8: Registration endpoint and JWT login/refresh endpoints
column12: Registering with an existing username returns 400 with a readable message;passwords are stored hashed - a plain-text password fails the DoD;login returns access and refresh tokens;an expired access token is refreshable
column13: US-1.1 register with username and password; US-1.2 log in with them. Already written with SimpleJWT (1 day / 7 day lifetimes, rotation on). Two things to finish: the route currently resolves to /api/api/auth/login/ (P-06 fixes the mount), and BLACKLIST_AFTER_ROTATION is set in settings while rest_framework_simplejwt.token_blacklist is not in INSTALLED_APPS - so rotation silently does not blacklist. G-04 depends on that being fixed.

column8: Message model and migration: sender, recipient, group, text, media FK, timestamps, ordering
column12: A message targets exactly one of a recipient or a group, never both;messages order chronologically;the migration exists and applies on an empty database
column13: US-2.1: 'As a logged-in user, I want to be able to send and receive messages with other users, so that I can have continuous and personal communication.' The model is written and the dual-target rule is already enforced in MessageSerializer.validate - but there is NO migration for it, so a fresh clone never gets the table. Generating that migration is the actual work here (P-03 covers the makemigrations run; this card owns the model shape being right first). Add the channel/topic target now rather than later - C-03 and US-2.3 need it.

column8: Message list/create/detail API, scoped so a user only sees conversations they belong to
column12: Requesting a conversation you are not part of returns 403, not an empty list;messages come back in chronological order;the endpoint is paginated
column13: US-2.5: 'As a user, I want to receive and view messages sent by others (in direct messages, groups or channels), so that I can stay up to date with conversations.' MessageListCreateView and MessageDetailView already exist and filter on ?user_id= / ?group_id=. Two gaps to close: with neither parameter the view returns everything the user can see rather than 403-ing on an out-of-scope request, and pagination is not configured.

column8: Shared message primitives - avatar, timestamp, message bubble, composer - used by the DM, group and channel views alike
column12: The DM view, the group view and the channel view all render through these components;there is exactly one message bubble implementation in the codebase, not three
column13: Three different chat surfaces are coming - DM (F-03), channel topic (F-05) and group (U-09) - and they are the same UI with a different fetch. Build the primitives once on day 1 so the other three are wiring, not re-implementation. Note that the existing wired components use Tailwind class names while Tailwind is not a dependency and no directives exist in index.css, so those classes currently render unstyled: either add Tailwind or use the semantic classes already in src/index.css.

column8: Chat view: message list with author and timestamp, plus the composer
column12: Messages render newest-last with author and time;the composer sends and clears;an empty conversation shows an empty state, not a spinner forever
column13: US-2.1 in the UI. Chat.jsx exists and already opens a WebSocket, but it imports '../../api' which does not resolve, and AuthContext never fetches the user so it sends user_id: undefined - which makes the consumer skip persisting the message while still broadcasting it. Rebuild it on the F-00 primitives and read history over REST (M-02); the socket is a Sprint 2 bonus, not this card.

The dashboard, dms, groups, channels, search, notifications and settings screens all navigate() to routes that do not exist, so the catch-all bounces them to /profile. Defining those routes is the work.

Fix that first; it is the acceptance criterion, not a nicety.

column13: US-3.3: 'As a regular user, I want to be able to delete my own sent message in a direct message, group or channel, so that an unnecessary or erroneous message is removed from the chat history.' column8: Search message text across DMs, groups and channels using PostgreSQL full-text search with a GIN index, scoped to the caller
column12: Results never include messages from conversations the caller is not in - verify by searching a term that only exists in a stranger's chat and confirming zero results;a search across a few thousand messages returns promptly;results say which conversation each hit is in

column8: Wire the search screen to the search API
column12: Typing a term and submitting returns real results;clicking a result opens that conversation at that message;no results shows an empty state

column8: Phase 2 report: requirement fulfilment, architecture alignment, deviations, ERD alignment, process summary

Start drafting on Aug 11, not Aug 12. Arman writes the architecture sections.

column12: An oversized file is rejected with a clear error;a disallowed type is rejected;the stored record captures type and size;the type recorded matches the file, not just the request header
column13: US-7.1 send images, video, audio or files in any direct or group message; US-2.4 attach them to a text message. Already written, with two defects to fix: MediaFileSerializer is defined twice in serializers.py (the second wins), and MediaUploadView.perform_create overwrites file_type with the HTTP content type, which defeats the model's own categorisation into image/video/audio/document.

column8: Media detail and serving endpoint, access-scoped to the conversation the media belongs to
column12: Requesting media from a conversation you are not a member of returns 403 - not the file;a direct URL guess does not bypass the check;media renders inline in the chat view
column13: US-7.2 is the channel-side version of US-7.1. The trap here is serving media as plain static files, which makes every upload world-readable to anyone who can guess a path - the access check has to be in front of the file. Depends on P-02 for the nginx location.

column8: Seed command producing users, conversations, groups, channels and sample media for testing
column12: One command on an empty database produces enough data to demo every story;it is idempotent or clearly refuses to run twice;the credentials it creates are printed
column13: seed_data already exists and makes three users and one group. Extend it to cover channels, topics, roles and media so the Review demo and INT-2's permission matrix have something to run against. Every clean-clone verification card depends on this working.

column8: Per-channel media restriction: uploading in a channel requires can_send_media, evaluated by the roles module
column12: With the restriction on, a member lacking can_send_media is refused by the API, not merely by a hidden button;the channel admin is never refused;DMs and groups are unaffected
column13: US-7.3: 'As a channel admin, I want to be able to restrict the ability to send media in my channel, so that I have greater control over the channel's content.' US-4.8 is the member-side half. The check must call roles.services.has_permission - if media_app decides this for itself, architecture.tex section 5.1 is broken and the report cannot honestly claim alignment.

column8: Group edit and delete, add and remove members honouring allow_invites, group-admin rights
column12: Adding a user whose allow_invites is off returns 403 and the user is not added;only the group admin may add, remove or delete;editing group name, image and description works
column13: US-5.2 group admin adds and removes members; US-6.3 delete the group; US-6.4 edit its information. user_stories_en.tex is explicit that the only difference between a group admin and a member is adding, removing and deleting others' messages - so do not invent a role system for groups; that is what channels are for. GroupAddRemoveMemberView exists but never checks allow_invites, which is the actual gap.

column8: Wire DirectMessages.jsx to the message API - real conversations, no mock data
column12: Two accounts in two browsers can exchange messages;a page refresh shows the full history;sending with an expired token refreshes and retries rather than silently failing
column13: US-2.1 and US-2.5 in the UI. Builds on Ali's U-03 layout and the F-00 primitives, reading M-02. This is the card the Sprint 1 Review demo hinges on, so if anything slips, protect this one.

column8: Channels dashboard wired to the channel API: list, create, open
column12: Creating a channel makes you its admin and it appears in the list;the list shows only channels you belong to;opening one navigates to its topics
column13: US-4.1 in the UI. ChannelsDashboard.jsx exists as a static mockup with an empty useState. Depends on C-02.

column8: Topic tabs and the channel message view, reusing the chat component
column12: Switching topics switches the message list;the create-topic control is hidden without can_create_topic and the API refuses it anyway;the same message bubble component as the DM view is used
column13: US-2.3 send and receive in a channel's topics; US-4.5 create topics. Depends on C-03 and on F-00 - the point of the primitives is that this card is wiring, not a third chat implementation.

column8: Group chat view
column12: Every group member can post and see each other's messages;the member list is visible;it renders through the same primitives as the DM and channel views
column13: US-2.2: 'As a member of a group, I want to be able to send and receive messages in the group, so that I can have continuous communication.' Moved to Amir because it is the third instance of the same chat surface and reuses F-00.

column8: WebSocket client with reconnect; live message rendering in all three contexts
column12: A message sent in one browser appears in the other with no refresh;dropping the connection reconnects without duplicating messages;the socket carries the auth token
column13: US-B1.1. Behind the Aug 11 gate. Chat.jsx already opens a raw WebSocket; the work is a single reusable client with reconnect and de-duplication, reading RT-02.

column8: Account and privacy settings screens wired to the profile and privacy endpoints
column12: Editing the profile persists and survives a reload;toggling allow_invites persists;a validation error from the API is shown, not swallowed
column13: US-10.1 edit your profile; US-5.4 control who can add you to a group or channel. All three screens exist as static mockups. Wire them to A-02 and A-03.

column12: Opening another user shows their display fields only;your own profile shows the edit affordance and theirs does not;a missing user shows a not-found state
column13: US-10.2: 'As a user, I want to be able to view other users' profiles, so that I can better identify my contacts in the system.' ViewProfile.jsx is a static mockup; EditProfile.jsx is already wired correctly and is the one component importing services/api.js properly. Reads M-03.

column8: Groups dashboard wired to the group API
column12: The list shows only groups you belong to;opening one navigates to its chat;an empty state is handled
column13: US-5.1 in the UI. GroupsDashboard.jsx exists as a static mockup with local useState. Reads A-06.

column13: Already built as a mockup. Reads A-06.

column12: The three event kinds from US-11.1 all appear;the unread badge matches the API;opening a notification marks it read and navigates to its subject
column13: US-11.1 covers a new message, being added to a group or channel, and a role change. NotificationsCenter.jsx exists as a static mockup with an empty array. Reads N-02.

column13: Cut for this release. US-B1.2 is the lowest-value half of the lowest-value bonus, and polling the N-02 endpoint gives the user almost the same thing. Parked and visible rather than quietly dropped, per methodology.md section 7.5.

column13: Cut for this release, together with its UI half F-08. If RT-02 lands early and the mandatory product is green, this is the first card to bring back.

column13: Cut for this release. M-05 delivers US-5.2 and US-6.4 server-side and they can be demonstrated against the API; a dedicated settings screen is the presentation of a requirement that is already met. Reinstate it if Sprint 2 runs ahead.
